summary: Nokia (NOKIA.HE, NASDAQ Helsinki) is a Finnish communication-equipment maker that is increasingly priced as an AI data-center networking provider; in this Valuatum equity research report dated 5 June 2026 we rate the stock SELL with a 12-month target price of 11.50 EUR against a current price of 13.90 EUR, implying roughly 17.2% downside. Market capitalisation is EUR 76 bn and enterprise value is EUR 74.7 bn.

The core valuation tension is a sharply bifurcated enterprise value. The Mobile Infrastructure segment generates roughly 73% of estimated 2026 group EBIT yet commands less than half of the group's EUR 74.7 billion enterprise value, while the Optical & IP Networks segment produces only about 28% of revenue and 31% of EBIT but is valued at EUR 35.5 billion (47.5% of EV) at an aggressive 49x EV/EBIT multiple on just EUR 725 million of 2026E EBIT.

On a reverse-valuation basis the embedded assumptions are demanding: to justify its EUR 35.5 billion allocation, Optical & IP Networks must grow revenue from EUR 5.8 billion to roughly EUR 9.0 billion while expanding EBIT margins from 12.5% toward 19%. With the whole group EV at 31.5x 2026E EBIT and priced for flawless execution in the hyperscaler optical market, we conclude the premium is fragile and reiterate the SELL call. The scenario base case implies EUR 13.43 per share, and a de-rating to a 20x hardware multiple could erase EUR 20.5 billion of EV and drive shares toward EUR 9.92.

thesis.title: Optical Networking Overvaluation
thesis.text: Nokia commands a massive EUR 74.7 billion enterprise value, driven heavily by its optical networking segment trading at an aggressive 49x multiple on just EUR 725 million in estimated earnings.

thesis.title: Stagnant Mobile Infrastructure
thesis.text: While mobile infrastructure provides a defensive EUR 1.73 billion in operating profit, traditional hardware deployment volumes remain stagnant, forcing the optical division to close a EUR 1.0 billion earnings shortfall.

thesis.title: Gross Margin Compression Risk
thesis.text: If alternative sourcing pressures gross margins, the aggressive optical multiple will contract violently to a mature 20x hardware average, potentially erasing EUR 20.5 billion in total enterprise value.

thesisBreaker: Flawless execution and massive scale in 800G and 1.6T coherent pluggables inside US hyperscalers drive sustained high-margin growth.

valuePools.name: Mobile Infrastructure
valuePools.economics: Revenue EUR 11,896m (57.1%) · Comp. EBIT EUR 1,728m (72.8% of EBIT, 14.5% margin) · EV EUR 36,839m
valuePools.text: Current profit engine generating roughly 73% of group EBIT but priced at a modest 21.3x EBIT multiple as a mature cash cow. Its 14.5% blended margin masks a ~4% hardware operating margin combined with the high-margin IP licensing business, which generates around EUR 1.5 billion of annual revenue at operating margins above 70%.

valuePools.name: Optical & IP Networks
valuePools.economics: Revenue EUR 5,800m (27.8%) · Comp. EBIT EUR 725m (30.6% of EBIT, 12.5% margin) · EV EUR 35,500m
valuePools.text: Scaling pool valued as Nokia's primary long-term growth engine at an aggressive ~49x EBIT multiple on AI data-center optionality. To support the EUR 35.5 billion allocation, the segment must grow revenue from EUR 5.8 billion to roughly EUR 9.0 billion over 3-5 years while expanding EBIT margins from 12.5% to about 19%, driven by Infinera integration and 800G/1.6T coherent pluggables.

valuePools.name: Fixed Networks
valuePools.economics: Revenue EUR 2,200m (10.6%) · Comp. EBIT EUR 169m (7.1% of EBIT, 7.7% margin) · EV EUR 2,400m
valuePools.text: Declining cash-flow pool assigned a low ~14x EBIT multiple amid post-pandemic revenue contraction. Nokia holds a dominant position in passive optical networking (PON) outside China; to justify its EUR 2.4 billion EV the segment merely needs to avoid margin collapse until US BEAD subsidies (USD 42.45 billion) accelerate deployment volumes.

reverseValuation.intro: The reverse valuation tests whether the revenue, margin and multiple assumptions embedded in Nokia's EUR 74.7 billion enterprise value are coherent, with the Optical & IP Networks segment as the sole variable driving major valuation swings while Mobile Infrastructure is held at its baseline maturity multiple. Because Nokia holds a net cash position of about EUR 1.5 billion, equity value modestly exceeds enterprise value.

coreAnalysis.heading: How the company creates economic value
coreAnalysis.text: Nokia operates a highly bifurcated economic model in which the source of operating profit diverges sharply from the source of enterprise value. Mobile Infrastructure generates roughly 73% of estimated 2026 group EBIT but commands less than half of the group's EUR 74.7 billion enterprise value, priced as a mature cash cow. By contrast, Optical & IP Networks generates only 28% of revenue and 31% of EBIT yet is valued at EUR 35.5 billion, or 47.5% of EV, reflecting an institutional pivot after the EUR 2.3 billion Infinera acquisition and soaring hyperscaler AI capex. The EUR 74,739 million enterprise value bridges to a EUR 75,950 million market cap via a EUR 1,527 million net cash position offset by EUR 316 million of other senior claims.

coreAnalysis.heading: Cross-pool bridge
coreAnalysis.text: The 2026 group forecast is driven by two opposing forces: structural stagnation in legacy telecom and explosive AI data-center growth. Net sales of EUR 20.8 billion are heavily supported by Mobile Infrastructure (over 57% of revenue), and group EBIT of EUR 2.37 billion depends on its high-margin patent licensing. At a historical 15x-17x telecom multiple, group EBIT would support only EUR 35-40 billion of enterprise value, versus the actual EUR 74.7 billion, which requires pricing Optical & IP Networks purely on future AI-networking optionality.

coreAnalysis.heading: Scenarios and verdict
coreAnalysis.text: The scenarios diverge entirely on the multiple assigned to Optical & IP Networks. In the downside, failure to capture hyperscaler share, supply-chain stalls or competition from Ciena and Arista compresses the segment multiple from 49x to a standard 20x hardware level, causing severe equity contraction toward EUR 9.78 per share. The upside requires flawless Infinera integration and massive 800G/1.6T scale, driving Optical EBIT toward EUR 2.0 billion and gross margins to 45%, supporting a EUR 50 billion segment valuation. With a group P/E above 43x, the stock is priced for execution perfection.

risks: Hyperscaler multi-sourcing commoditization (Optical & IP Networks): hyperscalers shift toward open architectures bypassing Nokia's proprietary DSPs, with gross-margin compression in optical components as the early warning - HIGH impact and a thesis-breaker if it occurs.

Indium phosphide supply-chain constraints (Optical & IP Networks): internal fabrication capacity fails to scale with hyperscaler demand, with stalled sequential revenue growth despite a high backlog as the early warning - MEDIUM impact, manageable.

RAN market-share loss to Ericsson (Mobile Infrastructure): pricing aggression from Ericsson leads to loss of key Western contracts, with loss of Tier-1 telecom replacement contracts in Europe as the early warning - MEDIUM impact, structural.

Patent licensing pricing pressure (Mobile Infrastructure): smartphone OEMs successfully litigate lower royalty rates globally, with extended litigation with major smartphone OEMs as the early warning - HIGH impact, structural.
catalysts: Hyperscaler capex announcements (near-term, Optical & IP Networks): continued growth above 20% year-over-year in AI infrastructure validates the TAM expansion supporting the Optical & IP valuation.

800G coherent pluggable shipments (medium-term, Optical & IP Networks): material volume confirmation inside US hyperscalers proves Infinera integration and competitive access; this is the most critical catalyst for the thesis.
Smartphone patent renewals (near-term, Mobile Infrastructure): no material price degradation in IP royalties secures the high-margin baseline cash flow.
Indium phosphide fab capacity (medium-term, Optical & IP Networks): resolution of wafer bottlenecks allows Optical & IP revenue growth to accelerate unconstrained.
